stories.title: Climate technology is already changing lives. Why isn’t it reaching more people?
stories.description:
In the foothills of the Himalayas, Nepali farmer Chiranjivi Acharya receives weather forecasts directly on his mobile phone. Behind these simple SMS messages is an artificial-intelligence-powered system that analyzes more than 30 years of weather data to predict local conditions and provide practical farming advice. 
Nepal is among the world’s most climate-vulnerable countries. And as climate change continues to disrupt rainfall patterns, Acharya and other farmers can no longer rely on traditional knowledge alone. For them, timely, location-specific forecasts and recommendations can make the difference between a successful harvest and a looming catastrophe of losing an entire season’s crops. 
Nepal’s example shows how simple technological solutions can help communities grappling with the growing impact of climate change. Many of these technologies already exist, and they are neither futuristic nor prohibitively expensive.  
As temperatures continue to rise, scaling up access to climate technology is an investment in human lives, food security and future economic opportunity.  
We all inhabit the same planet. And if one room in our shared home catches fire, the rest of us cannot simply close our doors and assume we will be safe. Climate change is a shared challenge, even if its consequences are profoundly unequal. That is why we must work together so people around the world have the tools they need to adapt and prepare.

stories.title: A novel three stage passive particle swarm optimization algorithm for the p-median problem
stories.description: The p-median problem (PMP) is a classical NP-hard problem in location science. To solve it, many methods have been developed, including a novel discrete particle swarm optimization (NDPSO). To further improve comprehensive performance of NDPSO, a novel three stage passive particle swarm optimization algorithm (TSPPSO for short) is proposed. In TSPPSO, first, an integer encoding scheme and random particle generation method are employed to form swarm particles. Second, a three-stage evolution strategy with single point crossover, single point mutation and a dynamic probability mechanism is developed. Third, a passive strategy for passive particles is also integrated into TSPPSO. To validate its effectiveness and advantage, a lot of experiments on 40 PMP instances are carried out. Related experimental results including comparisons with eight representative methods demonstrate the performance, simplicity, superiority and robustness of TSPPSO.
